label: First-token detector for a fixed subset of tokens (a c d f i n o p q s u v w 1 2)
explanation: Active at step 0, when the first original token is input, and only if that token is in a fixed set of 15: a c d f i n o p q s u v w 1 2. At t=0 it fires deterministically for these tokens and never for the other 15 (b e g h j k l m r t x y z 0 3). The input token sets the magnitude: d is strongest (about 0.68 of max), then u (about 0.45), then c (about 0.37), then f; the rest are weak (0.02-0.19). Remaining activations, about 19% of mass: (1) the first copy-phase input after <DEL> (recall_idx 1, where orig(0) is fed back in). For L=3 this produces the largest activations of all, up to max, e.g. d at about 1.0. It decays with L and is near zero for L>=6. (2) weak firing at t=1-2 on set tokens. Never fires on the <DEL> step or later in the copy phase.

issues: The core t=0 claim holds. (t==0)&isin(in_tok,SET) has precision 1.0 on both dev and test, and (t==0)&~isin(in_tok,SET) never fires (precision 0.0 over 50,080 steps).

The explanation of the recall_idx==1 misses is wrong. At L=3 the unit fires on 96.5% of recall_idx==1 steps for ANY fed-back token: 93% for tokens outside the 15-token set and 100% for tokens inside it. The token set does not gate it.

The L dependence is a hard cutoff, not a gradual fade. recall_idx==1 fires on 96.5% of steps at L=3, on 2.5% at L=4 (mass about 0.003), and exactly 0 at every L>=5. The claim that it 'shrinks as L grows and almost disappears for L>=6' is inaccurate.

The 'weak firing at t=1-2' is a systematic token-specific class, not scatter. (t==1)&in_tok==d fires with precision 1.0 (7.9% of activation mass), and (t==1)&in_tok==u with precision 0.75. Inputs w and v at t=1 never fire, so in_tok at t=1 reuses the same strong-token ordering (d > u > c > f).

The claim that adding a recall clause lowers F1 does not reproduce for the right clause. Adding (recall_idx==1)&(L==3) to the predicate raises dev F1 from 0.894 to 0.918 and mass recall from 0.80 to 0.88, with precision 0.998.
The label 'first-token detector' leaves out about 20% of activation mass that forms two clean, describable classes: the L=3 first copy-phase step (for any token) and a d/u input at t=1.
skeptic.revised_label: Early-sequence detector. Fires on the first input when it is one of a c d f i n o p q s u v w 1 2 (d strongest), also when the second input is d or u, and on the first copy-phase step of length-3 sequences (for any token).
